title: Count Subarrays With Fixed Bounds
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` and two integers `minK` and `maxK`. Count the contiguous, non-empty stretches of `nums` whose smallest element is exactly `minK` and whose largest element is exactly `maxK`, and return that count. Stretches at different positions count separately even when they hold the same values.
signature: long countSubarrays(int[] nums, int minK, int maxK)
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every start and end while tracking the running minimum and maximum works, but it is O(n²). Look instead at each end index `right` on its own. A start works when the stretch from it to `right` holds no value outside `[minK, maxK]` and contains at least one `minK` and one `maxK`. So the valid starts are a contiguous range: they begin just after the last out-of-range value and end at the earlier of the latest `minK` and latest `maxK` positions. Counting that range for every `right` is a variable-size sliding window whose left edge jumps past each bad value.

## Approach

1. Keep `badIndex`, `minIndex` and `maxIndex`: the last positions of an out-of-range value, of `minK` and of `maxK` (all `-1` at first).
2. Move `right` through `nums` and update whichever of the three positions `value` matches.
3. The starts that work for this `right` are `badIndex + 1` up to `Math.min(minIndex, maxIndex)`, so there are `validStarts = Math.min(minIndex, maxIndex) - badIndex` of them.
4. Add `validStarts` to `count` when it is positive and return `count` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 3, 5, 2, 7, 5]`, `minK = 1`, `maxK = 5`.

- `right = 0` (1): `minIndex = 0`, but no 5 yet, so `validStarts = -1 - (-1) = 0`.
- `right = 1` (3): still no 5, nothing added.
- `right = 2` (5): `maxIndex = 2`, `validStarts = min(0, 2) - (-1) = 1`, `count = 1` (`[1,3,5]`).
- `right = 3` (2): `validStarts = 1`, `count = 2` (`[1,3,5,2]`).
- `right = 4` (7): out of range, `badIndex = 4`, so `validStarts` is negative.
- `right = 5` (5): `maxIndex = 5` but `minIndex = 0 < badIndex`, nothing added. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each element is visited once with constant work.
- Space: O(1): only three positions and a counter are kept.

## Pitfalls

- When `minK === maxK` a single value updates both positions; the separate `if`s handle that, an `else if` would not.
- If `minK > maxK` no stretch qualifies; every `minK` is then above `maxK` and marks `badIndex`, so the count stays 0.
- Clamp at zero: `validStarts` is negative when the last bad value is newer than a needed bound.
- The count can reach about 5 · 10^9, which needs a 64-bit integer in Java and C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | number of fixed-bound subarrays found so far |
| `badIndex` | last index holding a value outside `[minK, maxK]` |
| `minIndex`, `maxIndex` | last indices holding `minK` and `maxK` |
| `right` | end index of the subarrays being counted |
| `validStarts` | how many start indices work for this `right` |

narration.3: No out-of-range value has been seen yet, so the window may start at index 0.
narration.4: minIndex will hold the latest position of minK.
narration.5: maxIndex will hold the latest position of maxK.
narration.7: Treat each index as the right end of the subarrays we count.
narration.9: A value outside [minK, maxK] can never sit inside a valid subarray.

narration.12: Seeing minK refreshes its latest position.
narration.15: Seeing maxK refreshes its latest position (both update when minK equals maxK).
narration.18: Any start after badIndex and no later than both bound positions works for this right end.
narration.19: A non-positive count means some bound is missing from the current window.
narration.20: Add every valid start for this right end.
narration.23: Every right end has been counted, so return the total.
